description: AstroDip is an interactive web dashboard that analyzes stellar light-curve data from NASA's TESS telescope . The platform allows users to scan star systems, visualize transit light curves, and run built-in validation simulations to confirm candidate signals against false-positive noise. Based on the consistency of the detected dips, Dip assigns a confidence score to each report, evaluating whether the signal is most likely a genuine planet or just space debris.
summary:
We developed AstroDip, an interactive Corona Transit & Exoplanet Detection Lab designed to analyze astronomical light curves and identify genuine exoplanets. Using live NASA TAP targets and custom MAST CSV uploads, AstroDip scans stellar photometry for brightness dips and combines Three.Js 3D orbital simulations with spectral and habitable-zone diagnostics.

AstroDip addresses the challenge of false positives in transit photometry where irregular dimming from circumstellar dust, disintegrating asteroids, or space debris mimics planetary transits. By evaluating dip symmetry, orbital periodicity, rocky core indicators, and JWST NIRSpec oxygen species bands, the platform assigns clear Exoplanet vs. Space Debris classification scores and a Life Possibility Index.

This tool is important because as space telescopes generate massive volumes of transit data, researchers and citizen scientists need accessible, transparent verification tools to filter out cosmic noise and prioritize truly habitable, Earth-like worlds for deeper atmospheric study.
details:
What AstroDip Does & How It Works

AstroDip is an interactive Corona Transit & Exoplanet Detection Lab designed to analyze astronomical light curves, verify transiting bodies, and evaluate exoplanet habitability. Users can select from real benchmark targets (such as Tabby’s Star, TRAPPIST-1e, Kepler-186f, K2-18b, and WD 1145+017b), fetch live targets via the NASA TAP (Table Access Protocol) service, or upload custom MAST (Mikulski Archive for Space Telescopes) CSV light curve datasets.

The platform processes stellar photometry through four integrated modules:

  • Scans light curves using adjustable Median Absolute Deviation (MAD Sigma) thresholds to measure dip depth (in ppm), signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), periodicity, and flux constancy.
  • Renders real-time interactive 3D orbital views and edge-on transit simulations synchronized with live stellar flux readings.
  • Distinguishes true planetary transits from false positives such as circumstellar dust clouds or disintegrating asteroid debris by analyzing light curve symmetry (e.g., symmetric U-shaped planetary dips vs. erratic, asymmetric V-shaped debris dips) and orbital regularity.
  • Calculates a Life Possibility Index by evaluating habitable zone (HZ) orbital parameters, rocky core indicators, and transmission spectra across JWST NIRSpec reference bands for five key oxygen species

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Transit photometry frequently encounters irregular dimming caused by comets, dust, or space debris. AstroDip provides transparent probability breakdowns (Exoplanet vs. Debris scores) to prevent misclassifying cosmic anomalies as planets.
  • By combining raw NASA archival data with intuitive 3D visualizations and instant habitability audits in a browser-based interface, AstroDip bridges the gap between complex astrophysical datasets and students, educators, and citizen scientists.
  • Helps researchers quickly screen candidate light curves and identify promising Earth-like or Hycean worlds worthy of high-demand telescope time (such as JWST atmospheric spectroscopy).

Tools, Technologies & Data Sources

  • HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, and Three.js for real-time 3D orbital mechanics and Milky Way spatial mapping.
  • NASA Exoplanet Archive (TAP API) for live target parameters, MAST light curve CSV datasets, and JWST NIRSpec reference spectral bands.
  • GitHub Pages (for live web deployment) and Canva (for mission presentation and visual design).

Creativity & Design Considerations

  • Rather than displaying static graphs alone, we paired mathematical dip detection (MAD Sigma and ppm metrics) with a synchronized 3D Edge-On Transit Verifier, allowing users to visually see why an asymmetric light curve corresponds to a dispersed debris cloud rather than a solid sphere.
  • Our team prioritized scientific interpretability (breaking down why a target passes or fails the Goldilocks Audit), flexibility (supporting both curated benchmark stars and custom user CSV uploads), and accessibility (ensuring the lab runs smoothly directly in a standard web browser with zero installation required).
